presets.name: Standard
presets.desc: Flat EQ with an 80 Hz high-pass: removes rumble and handling noise, changes nothing else
presets.notes: golem's Standard preset kept as is: the neutral starting point a hand-placed EQ gets

presets.name: Post-cab guitar cleanup
presets.desc: High-pass 90 Hz, steep low-pass 7 kHz, -3 dB at 350 Hz and a de-harsher: a cab sim sitting in a band mix
presets.notes: The two cuts every mixed guitar gets: lows go to the bass and kick, the fizz above 7 kHz is cab-sim air no mic hears

presets.name: Light guitar polish
presets.desc: High-pass 90 Hz, gentle 2 dB dip at 800 Hz, a touch of high shelf: a cleaner, slightly more open guitar
presets.notes: golem's Guitar polish kept as is

presets.name: Mid scoop
presets.desc: 5 dB cut at 550 Hz with a 2 dB high shelf: a hollower, wider-sounding crunch rhythm
presets.notes: golem's Mid scoop kept as is; proportional Q narrows the cut as it deepens, so the 1 kHz bite survives

presets.name: Deep V metal rhythm
presets.desc: Deep 7 dB cut at 750 Hz, lift at 90 Hz and 6 kHz, steep 9 kHz low-pass: the classic scooped thrash rhythm

refs.why: Mark IIC+ five-band graphic EQ set in a V, deepest cut near 750 Hz

presets.notes: Graphic-EQ V moved to bells; keeps 2.2 kHz pick attack so the scoop does not vanish in the band. Great alone, thin in a dense mix

presets.name: Tight mid push into the amp
presets.desc: Steep 140 Hz high-pass and +5 dB at 720 Hz, highs eased: tightens a high-gain amp's palm mutes from the front

refs.why: Misha Mansoor tightens his high-gain amps with an overdrive in front

presets.notes: Placed BEFORE the amp: an overdrive-pedal curve without the clipping. Less bass into the preamp = less flub; +3 dB out hits the input harder

presets.name: High-gain fizz tamer
presets.desc: Dynamic cut around 3.5 kHz plus a steep 8.5 kHz low-pass: removes fizz on sustained chords, keeps mute attack
presets.notes: The de-harsher is relative to the full band, so it reacts to fizz, not to loudness; the static 5.5 kHz dip handles cab-sim sizzle

presets.name: Solo mid lift
presets.desc: +4 dB broad bell at 1.2 kHz and +2 dB output: the lead steps forward of the band without more gain
presets.notes: Mids carry a guitar through a mix far better than volume or treble; put it on the solo scene, after the amp

presets.name: Parked wah lead
presets.desc: Narrow +12 dB resonant peak at 900 Hz, lows trimmed: a wah left half-open, nasal and vocal (EXP on Mid Freq)

refs.why: leads through a wah parked at one spot instead of rocked
half-open wah colouring his Ziggy-era lead tone

presets.notes: Constant Q (midprop 0) keeps the peak narrow; -5 dB output offsets the peak's added level. Assign EXP to midfreq to sweep it

presets.name: Bass clean-up
presets.desc: 35 Hz high-pass, 2 dB dip at 700 Hz, a hint of top: a cleaner bass DI that leaves room for the kick
presets.notes: golem's Bass clean-up kept as is

presets.name: Scooped slap bass
presets.desc: Low shelf +3 dB at 80 Hz, -5 dB at 500 Hz, bright shelf and air: thumb thump and pop with the mids out

refs.why: both-pickup Jazz bass slap with the mids scooped and the top open

presets.notes: The smile curve slap players dial; the de-harsher at 5 kHz catches the loudest pops so the bright shelf can stay up

presets.name: Vintage flatwound thump
presets.desc: Warm lift at 100 Hz, +2 dB at 700 Hz, highs rolled off from 4 kHz: an old P-bass with flats and tone down

refs.why: flatwound Precision with the tone rolled back on Motown sessions

presets.notes: The 700 Hz bump is the note definition that a P-bass keeps in a mix even when its top is gone

presets.name: Metal bass clank
presets.desc: Tight low end, -3 dB at 400 Hz, +5 dB at 2.2 kHz: a pick-attack clank that cuts through high-gain guitars
presets.notes: Low mids are the guitars' space; the bass is heard as sub plus upper-mid clank. Use after a bass drive or on the DI branch

presets.name: Acoustic stage anti-feedback
presets.desc: Steep 90 Hz high-pass, narrow -6 dB notch at 120 Hz, -3.5 dB piezo quack at 1.2 kHz, air: a piezo acoustic on stage
presets.notes: Body boom near 100-120 Hz is the first to feed back; sweep midfreq to the room's howl. The quack band varies (1-3 kHz) per pickup

presets.name: Vocal clarity
presets.desc: 120 Hz high-pass, -2.5 dB of box at 400 Hz, +2.5 dB high shelf: a clearer, less muddy live vocal
presets.notes: golem's Vocal clarity kept as is

presets.name: Airy live vocal
presets.desc: 100 Hz high-pass, -2.5 dB at 400 Hz, +3 dB air shelf at 12 kHz, de-ess around 6 kHz: open but never sharp
presets.notes: Presence comes from the air shelf, not 3-5 kHz, so stage monitors feed back less; the dynamic band acts as a de-esser

presets.name: Telephone band-pass
presets.desc: Steep high-pass 350 Hz and low-pass 3.4 kHz, +4 dB honk at 1.5 kHz: a voice through a phone or a tiny amp

refs.why: vocals sung through a small practice amp for a lo-fi, band-limited voice

presets.notes: 300 Hz-3.4 kHz is the phone line's band; the +4 dB output makes up most of the level the filters remove. Also works on drum loops

presets.name: Keys out of the bass's way
presets.desc: 120 Hz high-pass, -2 dB at 300 Hz, light lift at 2.5 kHz: piano or pad that sits above the bass and guitars
presets.notes: A full-range piano left hand fights the bass; raise lowcut to 200 Hz in a dense band, lower it for solo piano

presets.name: Dusty lo-fi keys
presets.desc: 90 Hz high-pass, warm lift at 150 Hz, steep 4.5 kHz low-pass and a dark tilt: keys that sound sampled from vinyl
presets.notes: Pair with a bitcrusher or tape wobble for the full effect; auto gain keeps it as loud as the bypassed keys

presets.name: Dark archtop warmth
presets.desc: -3 dB tilt around 1 kHz, gentle 6 kHz low-pass, loudness held by auto gain: a round, woody clean guitar
presets.notes: The tone-knob-at-3 sound without the volume drop; auto gain is static, so nothing pumps

presets.name: Boost-and-cut low end
presets.desc: +4 dB low shelf at 60 Hz with a broad -2 dB dip at 200 Hz: deeper thump, less box, for kick, bass or drum loops
presets.notes: The passive-console trick of boosting and cutting next to each other; the 25 Hz high-pass stops the shelf from feeding subsonic energy
